Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

speed noun

how fast something moves

also at full speed, at top speed, as fast as possible, velocity, swiftness, quickness

classical

Cic. Div. 2.144: celeritās et vīs equōrum (Lewis & Short)
Caes. B.G. 5.53: incrēdibilī celeritāte (Lewis & Short)

celeritās, celeritātis f.

noun, third declension

speed, quickness

The general word, of bodies, ships, news and minds (celeritās ingeniī). At full speed: quam celerrimē (Caes. B.G. 1.37.4) or summā celeritāte.

Other words

  • vēlōcitās, vēlōcitātis f. — speed of movement, fleetness

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.107: aliōs vidēmus vēlōcitāte ad cursum … valēre; Cic. Tusc. 4.31: vēlōcitās corporis celeritās appellātur (Lewis & Short)

    Speed of running and moving, of the body (Cicero, Caesar); of the mind only after Augustus (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s speed limit is vēlōcitātis modus (see limit).

Examples

  • nōn vīribus aut vēlōcitāte aut celeritāte corporum rēs magnae geruntur, sed cōnsiliō, auctōritāte, sententiā

    great things are not done by strength or speed or quickness of body, but by planning, authority and judgementCic. Sen. 17

  • cancrī in pavōre et retrōrsī parī vēlōcitāte redeunt

    when frightened, crabs run back, backwards, just as fastPlin. NH 9.98

  • Etiam celeritās in dēsīderiō mora est.

    When you long for something, even speed is slow.Publil. Syr. E 3

  • rē frūmentāriā quam celerrimē potuit comparātā magnīs itineribus ad Ariovistum contendit

    he got the corn supply together as fast as he could and marched at full stretch against AriovistusCaes. B.G. 1.37.4

See also quickly, hurry, limit.
